scope: A payment/acceptance comparison whose attached invoice provision does not support the acceptance half.

context.priorities: Compare invoice-receipt payment timing with the delivery-triggered acceptance window. This focused review does not cover total charges, change control or exit.

overview_items.text: The source gives conflicting invoice-payment periods: clause 2 says thirty days from receipt and Schedule A says seven days from receipt, without a stated priority rule resolving them.

findings.title: Payment and acceptance use different triggers
findings.facts: Schedule A permits invoicing when each deliverable is submitted and gives seven days from invoice receipt. Separately, the customer has ten business days after delivery to identify a material failure against the written scope, followed by supplier correction and resubmission.
findings.uncertainty: The thirty-day versus seven-day payment conflict remains unresolved; actual delivery and invoice-receipt dates are not supplied.
findings.suggested_question: Can the parties clarify the applicable payment period and record the delivery and invoice-receipt dates separately?

claim_issues.exact_claim: the customer has ten business days after delivery to identify a material failure against the written scope, followed by supplier correction and resubmission.
claim_issues.reason: The acceptance claim is true in clause 3 but the finding attaches only A2. Evidence attached to a different item cannot support this claim.

must_not_flag: Do not mark the ten-business-day acceptance rule as a source conflict.
Do not infer a payment deadline from the delivery dates or treat the practical clarification question as a contractual assertion.
